To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

combined inhibition of glutathione and thioredoxin metabolism using pharmacologically-relevant agents can enhance responses to radiation of human breast cancer cells and stem cells in vitro and in xenograft models.
combined inhibition of Trx- and GSH-dependent thiol metabolism enhanced radiation responses in breast and pancreatic cancer stem cells.
the combined inhibition of glutathione and thioredoxin metabolism enhances the responses of human breast and pancreatic tumors to radiation in vitro and in human tumor xenografted mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of glutathione, thioredoxin and glutathione peroxidase in cancer cell resistance to radiation and chemotherapy.
understanding how cancer cells survive radiation therapy and how to improve the effectiveness of this therapy.
understanding the mechanisms that regulate radiation responses in cancer cells and cancer stem cells, and developing strategies to enhance these responses by targeting thiol-dependent pathways.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
combined depletion of GSH and inhibition of TrxR activity can enhance radiation responses in breast cancer stem cells in vitro and in xenograft models.
combined inhibition of glutathione and thioredoxin-dependent thiol metabolism can enhance the radiation response of human breast cancer cells in vitro and in human breast cancer xenograph models.

combined inhibition of TrxR and GSH metabolism using pharmacologically achievable concentrations of Au and BSo, respectively, can enhance radiation responses in breast cancer cells in vitro and in human breast cancer xenographs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel strategy that can be used to enhance radiation responses in breast cancer stem cells.
combined targeting of GSH and TRX metabolism can enhance the efficacy of radiotherapy for breast cancer stem cells.
combined targeting of glutathione and thioredoxin metabolism can significantly enhance radiation responses in breast cancer stem cells in vitro and in human breast cancer xenographs in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

inhibition of GSH-dependent metabolism can enhance radiation responses of breast cancer stem cells, and that combined inhibition of Trx- and GSH-dependent metabolism using pharmacologically achievable doses of Au and BSo can significantly enhance the survival of mice bearing breast cancer xenografted with human breast cancer cells.
the combination of drugs that inhibit GSH and thioredoxin metabolism can significantly increase the sensitivity of human breast cancer cells to radiation in vitro and in human tumor xenografted mice.
inhibition of GSH-dependent metabolism using BSO and inhibition of thiols metabolism using Au can enhance responses of cancer stem cells to ionizing radiation.
